text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easier for others to use. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. This helps developers understand what happened. Good documentation is also important, because it explains how each endpoint works and what data it needs. Finally, use versioning, for example /api/v1/, so you can update your API without breaking existing applications. Following these practices keeps your API clean, reliable, and easy to maintain over time.
